input.persona: curious, friendly first-time user with a few minutes to spare
input.guidance: Begin by asking what this assistant is for and what it can help you with. Then ask what kinds of requests it handles most often, and for one or two concrete examples. If it offers a menu or lists specific options, pick the one that sounds most central and try it — make a simple, benign request of that kind and see how it responds. Ask who it's meant to serve (customers? employees? anyone?). Ask whether there is anything it can't do or won't help with. If it mentions actions or lookups it can perform, ask what it would need from you to do one. Close by thanking it and asking how most people usually get started.

result: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion. Nothing is judged; the transcript is analyzed by reps-explore to draft the agent profile.

input.persona: friendly first-time user who arrived with a task in mind but isn't sure this is the right assistant
input.guidance: Begin by saying you're not sure you're in the right place, and describe — vaguely, without naming a domain — that you 'need help sorting something out'. Ask the assistant what it would need to know to help. Let it lead: answer its clarifying questions briefly and vaguely, and note what it asks for. Then ask directly: 'so what exactly are you set up to help with?' Ask for an example of a request it recently handled well. Ask whether it can take actions on your behalf or only answer questions. Close by thanking it.

result: Discovery conversation — no pass criterion. Nothing is judged; the transcript is analyzed by reps-explore to draft the agent profile.

input.persona: polite, slightly cautious first-time user who wants to know the rules before starting
input.guidance: Begin by asking what this assistant is NOT able to help with — what's out of scope or against its rules. Ask what happens if someone asks for something it can't do (does it hand off to a person?). Ask whether it needs to verify who you are before helping, and what that involves. Then flip to the positive: ask what it CAN do and for its two or three most common requests. Ask if there are topics it must avoid entirely. Close by thanking it and saying you'll come back with a real request.
